source_text:
Contra Severum Antiochenum (fragmentum ap. Pseudo-Anastasium
Sinaitam, Contra monophysitas)
89.1189 Ὀλυμπιοδώρου τοῦ μεγάλου φιλοσόφου διακόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας, ἐκ τοῦ
δευτέρου λόγου τοῦ κατὰ Σεβήρου, ἐν ᾧ παραγαγὼν τὴν χρῆσιν τοῦ ἁγίου
Ἀθανασίου τὴν λέγουσαν τὰ δύο θελήματα ἐπὶ Χριστοῦ, οὕτω πως διεξέρχεται
λέγων·
thought_title: Introductory lemma to Olympiodorus's citation of Athanasius
orientation: This is the opening lemma of a fragment from Olympiodorus's second book against Severus, introducing a quotation from Athanasius about two wills in Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Of Olympiodorus the great philosopher, deacon of Alexandria, from the second book of the work against Severus, in which, having brought forward the quotation of Saint Athanasius that says the two wills in Christ, Olympiodorus expounds it in some such way, saying:

choices.why: The glossary specifies 'book' for λόγος in the sense of a division of a multi-part work, and the context is the second book of a treatise.
The glossary specifies 'quotation' for χρῆσις in the sense of a cited passage from an authority.
The glossary specifies 'wills' for θελήματα, referring to the two wills in Christ.
The participle indicates introducing or adducing the quotation, fitting the lemma's report that Olympiodorus cited Athanasius.
The verb means to go through in detail or explain, matching the lemma's statement that Olympiodorus discussed the passage.

pass_b_english: From the second book of Olympiodorus, the great philosopher and deacon of Alexandria, against Severus. In it, after bringing forward the quotation from Saint Athanasius that speaks of two wills in Christ, he expounds it in this way, saying:
